description.narrative: AHRI works to meet the reseach and capacity building demands of Ethiopia in biomedical fields. The aim of the current application is to work in areas of high quality research, capacity building towards national competence, information dicemination, innovation for "more health for the money" concept, and to strengthen AHRI as an institution in order to maintain already strong competencies.

Insatsen syftar till att stärka AHRI som ett centrum för forskning inom biomedicin, samt att stödja forskarutbildning av hög kvalité genom kunskapsöverföring i samarbete med svenska universitet. Insatsen har 5 mål: 1) Forskning av hög kvalité, 2) Kapacitetsuppbyggnad för nationell kompetens för evidensbaserat beslutsfattande inom hälsoområdet, 3) spridning av forskningsresultat för användning i policy och praktik, 4) innovationer för ökad effektivitet inom hälsoområdet samt 5) stärkande av AHRI som institution. AHRI är ansvarigt för genomförandet av insatsen, med stöd av svenska universitet för doktorandutbildning samt med medel från andra internationella forskningsinstitutioner. Insatsens totala budget är SEK 49,996,906.

The overarching goal of this intervention is to "contribute to Ethiopia's ability to provide best health services to its citizens at any given time". The intermediate goal is to "make Ethiopia highly competent to organize relevant research for good health policies and practices." Outcomes are expected in five core intervention areas within the programme: a) high quality, quickly adaptive research; b) National competence capacity building; c) information dissemination, promoting research relevance and use; d) Innovation for more health for the money; and e) AHRI institution strengthening.

AHRI has achieved the goals set, both long- and short-term goals.
The Ethiopian government has taken over and provides funding to AHRI. AHRI now has students from all over the country and has established partnerships both in Africa, the latest being an MOU signed with University of Rwanda on Vaccine manufacturing.
AHRI's goal of institutional strengthening has also been achieved, according to the annual report. AHRIs new laboratory complex building, funded by the govt. of Ethiopia, is progressing as per project plans, this is a critical component to achieving improved capacity and effectiveness of institutional infrastructure.
The Clinical Research Network (CRN) expanded its members to 13 local universities including Addis Ababa, Haramaya, Gondar, Hawassa, Mekelle, Arbaminch, Debremarkos, Debrberhan, Arsi, Ambo and Semera universities as well as Saint Paul Hospital Millennium Medical College.
AHRI is already contributing to Ethiopia's ability to provide best health services to its citizens at any given time through their training for Human Resources for Health. as well as their research in both communicable and noncommunicable diseases. They have well established research facilities and research partners globally, attracting excellent researchers from respected universities around the globe. They also publish their research in some of the high impact journals hence making AHRI an attractive partner in the field of medicine and health in general.
